prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a sideswipe while changing lanes claim. Injury: back strain. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1021; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened following report of a sideswipe collision during a lane change. Insured reports the other vehicle drifted into their lane on the right side. Both drivers are on scene with minor body damage visible on the driver side panel. Photos requested from both parties.

Entry 2: Spoke with the claimant by phone. Claimant reports neck and lower back pain starting the day after the collision and is seeking medical evaluation. Claimant is not represented by an attorney and has not yet provided a written statement. Explained the claims process and the documents needed to proceed.

Entry 3: Reviewed submitted photos and a dash camera clip from the insured vehicle. The clip shows the other vehicle moving laterally into the adjacent lane while the insured was already positioned in that lane. Preliminary liability assessment leans toward the other driver, pending witness statements.

Entry 4: Claimant provided a medical note indicating a back strain diagnosis with a recommended course of physical therapy and follow-up in two weeks. No fractures or internal injuries reported. Injury reserve adjusted to reflect the documented treatment plan. Sent claimant a copy of the injury claim form.

Entry 5: Follow-up call with claimant to confirm receipt of the forms and to ask about any missed work or out-of-pocket expenses. Claimant is cooperative and will return documentation within the week. Liability review remains open pending the final witness statement. Next review scheduled for the following week.
